basic_information.name: Sir Syed University of Engineering & Technology

admissions.eligibility_criteria: Applicants must have completed (or be completing) Intermediate/A-Levels/High School Diploma/IB or an equivalent qualification by around June 2026, and must meet program-specific grade/subject requirements listed on HU's Admissions Criteria page.
admissions.admission_process: Register online → Complete e-application → Submit before deadline → Pay application fee → Appear for entrance exam → Shortlisted applicants attend interview → Complete Meta-curricular Experience Form as part of the compulsory application section.
admissions.merit_calculation_method: Based on entrance exam performance, interview evaluation, and application review.
admissions.interview_requirement: Required for shortlisted applicants after the entrance exam

entry_tests.passing_criteria: No negative marking. Test is adaptive — adjusts difficulty based on performance.
entry_tests.sample_pattern: DSSE (engineering/sciences) applicants: Advanced Level Mathematics with ~20-25 questions covering equations, functions, geometry, and trigonometry. AHSS (humanities/social sciences) applicants: Arithmetic — basic operations, fractions, decimals, percentages, and estimation.
entry_tests.preparation_tips: The exam is a standardized test developed by the College Board, assessing English proficiency and Math competence. DSSE applicants face advanced math; AHSS applicants face arithmetic-level math. All applicants may qualify for exemption based on SAT I scores or high grades. Registering early can earn a discount on the enrollment fee and eligibility for the HU Summer Program. Applicants from Sindh test in Karachi; those outside Sindh can use test centers elsewhere.

fees.fee_notes: Full tuition is approximately PKR 450,000/semester (Class of 2030, 2026-27). Most students receive some scholarship/aid. Approximate third-party estimates by program: SAHSS ~PKR 285,000-315,000/semester, Engineering ~PKR 350,000-395,000/semester, Computer Science ~PKR 335,000-370,000/semester. Fees payable in two installments per semester. A 5% prepayment discount is available if paid annually upfront without scholarship/aid. Refund policy: 100% refund before classes begin or within first 7 days; 50% refund days 8-15; no refund after day 15.

scholarships.eligibility: Based on secondary school grades and entrance exam/SAT performance — not grades alone.
scholarships.coverage_type: 100% financial support for all four years
scholarships.renewable_conditions: Renews automatically each semester for up to four years, subject to conditions.

scholarships.eligibility: Based on secondary school grades and entrance exam/SAT performance — not grades alone. Financial aid amount is need-based and personalized per admitted student.
scholarships.renewable_conditions: Renews automatically each semester for up to four years, subject to conditions.

scholarships.eligibility: Based on secondary school grades and entrance exam/SAT performance. Around 80-85% of students receive some form of scholarship or financial aid.
scholarships.coverage_type: Up to 50% of tuition and lab/studio fees
scholarships.renewable_conditions: Renews automatically each semester for up to four years, subject to conditions.

placements.placement_support: Students can work on campus via the Student Employment Portal (TA, peer tutor, library assistant, etc.) from Semester II onward, given a minimum CGPA.

faqs.question: What qualifications do I need to apply to Habib University?
faqs.answer: Applicants must have completed (or be completing) Intermediate/A-Levels/High School Diploma/IB or an equivalent qualification by around June 2026, and must meet program-specific grade/subject requirements listed on HU's Admissions Criteria page.

faqs.question: What does the HU entrance exam look like?
faqs.answer: The exam is computer-based, approximately 3.5 hours long, testing English (Reading, Writing, Essay) plus Math, with no negative marking. The test is adaptive — it adjusts question difficulty based on your performance. DSSE applicants are tested on Advanced Level Mathematics (~20-25 questions), while AHSS applicants are tested on Arithmetic.

faqs.question: Can I be exempted from the entrance exam?
faqs.answer: Yes, applicants may qualify for exemption based on SAT I scores or high grades. Check the official admissions page for specific exemption criteria.

faqs.question: What percentage of students receive scholarships?
faqs.answer: Around 80-85% of students receive some form of scholarship or financial aid. Key programs include HU TOPS (100% support), HU EOP (up to 80%), and other scholarships covering up to 50% of tuition and lab/studio fees.

faqs.question: What is the fee structure for 2026-27?
faqs.answer: Full tuition is approximately PKR 450,000 per semester (most students are on some scholarship/aid). Fees are payable in two installments per semester, and a 5% prepayment discount is available if you pay annually upfront without scholarship/aid.

faqs.question: What is the refund policy?
faqs.answer: 100% refund if requested before classes begin or within the first 7 days; 50% refund from day 8-15; no refund after day 15.

faqs.question: Can I work on campus as a student?
faqs.answer: Yes, students can work on campus via the Student Employment Portal (TA, peer tutor, library assistant, etc.) from Semester II onward, given a minimum CGPA.

faqs.question: Are student loans available?
faqs.answer: Yes, financial aid amount is need-based and personalized per admitted student, with student loan facilitation also available.

admissions.admission_months: Two intakes per year: Fall and Spring
admissions.application_deadline: Fall 2026: application window ran through late June 2026
admissions.result_date: Merit lists (1st, 2nd, 3rd, and final) published on the result portal
admissions.eligibility_criteria: Admission is strictly merit-based; FAST does not accept ECAT or NTS scores for undergraduate admissions — every applicant must sit FAST's own NU Entry Test (unless exempted via a qualifying SAT-I/GRE score). Candidates with a qualifying SAT-I (Reasoning) score can skip the entry test, subject to cut-off thresholds; if both scores exist, the better one is used. GRE is accepted as an alternative for MS/PhD applicants (subject to percentile thresholds).
required_documents: Roll number slip (downloaded before the test date)
admissions.admission_process: Create an account on the admissions portal using a valid CNIC/B-form → Select program level (BS or PG/Postgraduate) → Fill in academic information → Generate and pay the test fee challan (~Rs. 1,500) via bank or online payment → Download your roll number slip → Sit the NU Entry Test (or submit qualifying SAT-I/GRE scores in lieu of it) → Check merit lists (1st, 2nd, 3rd, and final). Applicants may apply to multiple campuses and programs simultaneously.
admissions.merit_calculation_method: 50% FAST Entry Test score + 40% HSSC/FSc (or equivalent) marks + 10% SSC marks

entry_tests.passing_criteria: ~120 MCQs (Adv. Math 50, Basic Math 20, IQ 20, English 30) with negative marking of -0.25 per wrong answer — confirm the current marking scheme on the official sample paper before test day. Each of the four sections is individually timed; once a section's timer ends (or it's submitted), you cannot return to it.
entry_tests.sample_pattern: BSCS / BS Engineering format: Advanced Mathematics 50%, Basic Mathematics/Quantitative 20%, IQ & Analytical Reasoning 20%, English Comprehension & Grammar 10%. Business programs (BBA etc.) use the same MCQ, timed format but weight more toward English, Basic Mathematics, and Analytical/Logical Reasoning rather than advanced/engineering math.
entry_tests.preparation_tips: Official sample papers on nu.edu.pk are the primary reference; third-party past-paper compilations (Wondar, QuizWing, Dogar Brothers, Maqsad, Parhlai) vary in accuracy/currency.

entry_tests.sample_pattern: MBA/MS (AF) test windows are typically scheduled separately from the BS cycle (e.g., one recent cycle ran 7–18 July). Same MCQ, timed format, weighted toward English, Basic Mathematics, and Analytical/Logical Reasoning.

fees.fee_notes: Estimates vary significantly by source, campus, and year — verify directly with the admissions office before depositing any challan. Tuition per credit hour cited as: Rs. 8,500 (Source A, uniform across BS/MS/PhD for 2026); ~Rs. 10,000 (Source B, ~Rs. 150,000–180,000/semester for 5–6 courses); ~Rs. 9,500 (Source C, lab-intensive courses may cost extra); Rs. 7,500 at the Lahore campus (plus Rs. 1,000/credit hour lab fee). Other one-time/recurring charges commonly cited: one-time Admission Fee ~Rs. 15,000–30,000; Refundable Security Deposit ~Rs. 20,000; Student Activity Fee ~Rs. 1,000/semester; Examination Fee ~Rs. 3,000/semester; Miscellaneous fee (transcript, rechecking, campus transfer, retake, late registration — non-refundable) ~Rs. 2,500/semester; Hostel fee ~Rs. 25,000/semester; Transport fee ~Rs. 8,000/semester; PhD monthly fellowship stipend ~Rs. 60,000 (where applicable). A typical BS degree (130 credit hours over 8 semesters) is often estimated in the Rs. 1.6 million+ total range, though this varies widely by campus and year. Confirm current figures directly with FAST via nu.edu.pk before treating them as final.

scholarships.eligibility: Partial to full tuition fee waivers for students who can demonstrate genuine financial need. Can be applied for during admission or later via the student portal. Eligibility considers both academic performance in prior qualifications (SSC/HSSC) and admission test score.
scholarships.coverage_type: Partial to full tuition fee waiver
scholarships.renewable_conditions: Applying simultaneously with your application (not after) is recommended.

scholarships.eligibility: Awarded to top-ranked students on the merit list; described by some sources as limited in availability. Eligibility considers both academic performance in prior qualifications (SSC/HSSC) and admission test score.
scholarships.coverage_type: Merit award for top-ranked students on the merit list
